background.title: Ethiopian civil conflict (2018–present)
background.description: Period of civil conflict and unrest in Ethiopia during Abiy Ahmed's tenure
background.extract: The Ethiopian civil conflict is a series of armed conflicts in Ethiopia that have been ongoing since 2018. In November 2019, three of the four constituent parties of the ruling Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF) approved a merger into the Prosperity Party, while the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) opposed the move. After the 20-year border conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea, a decade of internal tensions, two years of protests, and a state of emergency, Hailemariam Desalegn resigned on 15 February 2018 as prime minister and EPRDF chairman, and there were hopes of peace under his successor Abiy Ahmed. However, war broke out in the Tigray Region, with resurgent regional and ethnic factional attacks throughout Ethiopia. The civil wars caused substantial human rights violations, war crimes, and extrajudicial killings.

headlines.title: Ethiopian PM puts ministers through military training
headlines.excerpt: The prime minister has previously emphasised military preparedness as central to his government's ambitions.

headlines.title: Drone strikes in Ethiopia kill at least 25: witnesses
headlines.excerpt: Multiple drone strikes have hit northern regions of Ethiopia since Thursday, killing at least 25 civilians, including children, witnesses and a medical source said on Friday

headlines.title: Gunfire heard across Ethiopia border as growing numbers flee into Kenya
headlines.excerpt: Gunfire echoes across the Ethiopia-Kenya border in Moyale, as violence drives thousands to flee into Kenya. The clashes stem from a territorial dispute between Ethiopia’s Oromia and Somali regions.

headlines.title: World News in Brief: Aid for Ethiopia, Abyei drone strikes condemned, extreme heat and newborn health
headlines.excerpt: The World Health Organization (WHO) is scaling up emergency health response operations across Afar, Amhara and Tigray in Ethiopia to address growing humanitarian and health needs resulting from ongoing hostilities.
